sections.h2: What is the fastest path to a closing in Homestead?
sections.html:
Choose how you will sell, get title and lien paperwork in order, and sign a deed that is witnessed, taxed and recorded in Miami-Dade County. The buyer and the state of your title set the pace, since no one gets to skip recording.

Sellers in South Dade tend to weigh three routes. Listing publicly reaches the most people yet depends on a lender's appraisal. A cash purchase drops the lender and often the repair negotiation, a good fit for a house needing work. Selling to family is permitted, but a transfer for money still owes deed tax, and estate-planning transfers have no separate exemption.

  • Check who is on title, including any owner who has died or moved away.
  • Request a payoff letter from every lender on the house.
  • Get the current tax bill and look for unpaid earlier years.

Buyers here skew young and family-oriented, and renting is common. Population rose from 60,512 in 2010 to 80,737 in 2020, with 86,242 estimated for mid-2025. Only 48.3 percent of homes are owner-occupied, which lets rentals edge ahead. A typical owner-occupied house is worth $380,000, and the middle rent is $1,674. Households average 3.21 people. About 68.8 percent of residents use another language at home, so bilingual listings and documents can help.

The city took a direct hit from Hurricane Andrew in 1992, so keep permit history and insurance claim paperwork on hand for the buyer and the title company. Recent public projects include a voter-approved downtown revitalization in 2014, the reopened Seminole Theatre in 2015, a new City Hall in 2016 and the Cybrarium library in 2021, while the Speedway and the air force base, reestablished in 1953, remain big local anchors. Homestead also has designated historic districts and a historic downtown, which means a call to the city comes first if an older building is to be altered.

sections.h2: Selling a former or current rental
sections.html:
Many sellers in Homestead are landlords or heirs who never lived in the house, which shapes both the tax story and what buyers ask.

The county appraiser cautions owners against jeopardizing a homestead exemption by renting the property. An exemption claimed during a rental period can lead to back taxes covering ten years, plus 15 percent annual interest and a 50 percent penalty. Talk to a Florida attorney before you sell.

With a tenant in place, put the lease in the buyer's hands early. Chapter 83 sets 30 days of notice for a tenancy by the month, and an unpaid-rent demand lasts three days, not counting weekends and court holidays.

sections.h2: Deed tax and who must sign
sections.html:
A Homestead deed is taxed under Miami-Dade's own schedule. The base is 60 cents on each $100, and a 45 cent surtax on each $100 sits on top, except when the document conveys nothing but a single-family dwelling. Seventy cents is the figure in every other county.

Because of that exception, the kind of property matters. A single-family house generally avoids the surtax, but a duplex does not qualify. Let your closing agent confirm which treatment applies.

The contract may assign the tax to one side, yet everyone who signs stays liable for it, and the clerk is paid when the deed is filed. Recording starts at $5.00 for page one under section 28.24. The deed itself must be written and have two subscribing witnesses, who may appear by audio-video.

Your exemption stops at closing. Each new owner files alone, and the filing date is March 1. The TRIM notice shows how long late filings are taken, typically until 25 days after it is mailed, and a petition to the Value Adjustment Board may carry a $15 fee.

A ballot measure, Amendment 3, was approved November 3, 2026. If a buyer set up Florida residency by December 31, 2026, the largest non-school exemption becomes $150,000 for tax year 2027, then $250,000 for 2028. People who arrive later follow separate rules, and the school-board piece remains $25,000. The appraiser can say how it affects your buyer.

The first January 1 after closing, the parcel is reassessed at just value, which can make the buyer's opening bill larger than yours. Growth from there is held to the lesser of 3 percent or the CPI change.

• Foreclosure: the clerk auctions the house 20 to 35 days after final judgment, though the plaintiff may agree to wait.
  • Probate: a death over two years back, or a small estate with non-exempt value up to $150,000, may qualify for summary administration.
  • Tax certificates: an unredeemed certificate lets its holder ask for a tax deed after two years, counted from April 1 of the issue year. Pay off old balances first.

Florida has no estate tax on a death after 2004.

sections.h2: A checklist for landlords and heirs
sections.html:
Inherited the house, or renting it out? Title comes first. See who is named on the deed, and if an owner has died, learn who may sign for the estate. Next, pull together each lease, rent record and tenant phone number, which any serious buyer will request. Then ask the county Property Appraiser whether a homestead exemption stayed in place during any rental period, since that is where back taxes can arise.

Once you have those answers, line up offers by what you would net. Offers differ in how much time they need. One buyer may keep your tenants and move fast, another may want the keys free and clear. A cash buyer who accepts the house as it sits can spare you repair bills and a lender's schedule.

sections.h2: What a cash sale skips in Homestead
sections.html:
Without a lender, a South Dade cash deal avoids an underwriter's calendar and a bank's repair list. Owners usually notice three differences: fewer showings, less haggling over the inspection report, and a closing day set by agreement. Title work, payoffs and recording stay the same, and so does the deed tax.

Houses with an aging roof, storm damage, tenants or a stalled estate often suit that route. Weigh any cash figure against a listing's likely net after repairs, commissions and carrying costs, and obtain proof of funds and written terms before signing.

sections.h2: From accepted offer to recorded deed
sections.html:
After acceptance the closing agent opens title work and requests a payoff figure from each lender. The agent checks the tax bill for unpaid earlier years, drafts the deed and schedules the two witnesses. Any balance owed to the tax collector comes out of your proceeds at the table.

The deed is recorded at the clerk's office, which also takes the stamp tax. Speed turns on the clerk's queue and on whether your agent files electronically. Title cleanup and recording take time even in a cash sale, so settle on a written timeline before naming a closing day.

faqs.q: Is the deed tax different in Homestead?
faqs.a: It is, since Miami-Dade runs its own schedule. A 45 cent surtax on top of the base rate is skipped when the deed moves only a single-family dwelling.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Homestead house with a tenant inside?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer steps into the lease, so share it early. Ending a month-to-month tenancy takes 30 days' statutory notice.

faqs.q: Does the buyer get my exemption?
faqs.a: No. The buyer files separately by March 1, and value resets on the change of ownership.

faqs.q: How are unpaid property taxes handled?
faqs.a: They come out of your proceeds at closing. Get the exact balance from the county tax collector, since an unpaid bill turns delinquent April 1.

faqs.q: How long does the deed take to record?
faqs.a: The clerk's office records it and collects the stamp tax. Timing depends on the clerk's queue and on electronic filing by your closing agent.
